title: Polynomial-time independent set under a forbidden forest
formal: For every fixed finite forest \(H\) whose connected components each have at most three leaves, does Maximum Weight Independent Set on \(H\)-free graphs admit a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm? Precisely, must there exist an algorithm \(A_{H}\) and constants \(c_{H},C_{H}>0\) that, for every \(H\)-free vertex-weighted graph \((G,w)\) of encoding length \(L\), output a maximum-weight independent set in at most \(C_{H}(L+1)^{c_{H}}\) steps?

context:
The sources recall that forbidding a fixed graph outside this forest family leaves Maximum Weight Independent Set NP-hard. Polynomial algorithms for every forest in the family would identify the tractable side of the classification for a single forbidden induced subgraph.

Theorem 1.3 of the September 2025 full version gives an algorithm for every such fixed \(H\), with graph-size running time \(n^{O_{H}((\log n)^{19})}\). This is major progress over the earlier subexponential and approximation results, but its exponent still grows with \(n\). Conjecture 1.1 in that same version retains the polynomial target.

The consolidated STACS 2024 source proves polynomial-time solvability when \(G\) excludes both an induced \(S_{t,t,t}\) and a fixed complete bipartite graph \(K_{s,s}\) as an ordinary subgraph. Its Conjecture 10 asks about replacing the biclique restriction by a clique restriction. Both restrictions are additional to the general question on this card.

The 2025 MFCS paper improves the structural theorem behind the quasipolynomial algorithms and simplifies polynomial algorithms in sparse cases. It still describes polynomial-time solvability for the full family as conjectural.
why: This conjecture would complete a natural complexity classification of a central optimization problem by forbidden induced structure. It asks whether the large family now admitting quasipolynomial algorithms actually permits polynomial-time exact optimization, including graphs of unrestricted density.
status_note: Read the original full-family paragraph, the consolidated 2024 sparse theorem and Conjecture 10, the September 2025 full quasipolynomial version, and the 2025 MFCS introduction. Checked the apparently broader polynomial manuscript on the author’s site: the linked PDF is explicitly bounded-degree. Searches through 12 September 2026 found no polynomial algorithm for the complete family.

references.title: Max Weight Independent Set in Sparse Graphs with No Long Claws
references.authors: Abrishami, Tara; Chudnovsky, Maria; Pilipczuk, Marcin; Rzążewski, Paweł
references.locator: STACS 2024, article 4: graph/weight conventions in Section 1, Theorems 1–2 and Conjecture 10 read. S_{t,t,t} is excluded as an induced subgraph. The proved theorem additionally excludes a fixed biclique as a subgraph.

definitions:
Graphs are finite, undirected and simple. A forest has no cycle. In a nontrivial tree, a leaf has degree one; an isolated vertex is allowed as a component. A tree with at most three leaves is a path or a subdivided claw. A subdivided claw \(S_{a,b,c}\), for integers \(a,b,c\geq1\), consists of three internally disjoint paths of respectively \(a,b,c\) edges sharing one endpoint. That common endpoint has degree three, and the other endpoints are the three leaves.

The graph \(G\) is \(H\)-free if no vertex subset induces a graph isomorphic to \(H\). An induced copy must preserve both edges and nonedges. If \(H\) is disconnected, all its components must occur together with no extra edges between their chosen vertices. Excluding the whole forest is therefore not the same as separately excluding every component.

The input explicitly lists \(G\) and nonnegative integer vertex weights \(w(v)\), encoded in binary. The length \(L\) includes the graph and all weight bits; zero weights and the empty independent set are allowed. An independent set \(I\subseteq V(G)\) contains no pair joined by an edge. Its weight is
\[w(I)=\sum_{v\in I}w(v).\]
The required output is a set \(I\) attaining the largest possible weight, not merely an inclusion-maximal set or an approximation.

The forbidden graph \(H\) is fixed before the input varies. The algorithm, polynomial exponent and multiplicative constant may depend on \(H\). The question does not require one exponent independent of \(H\), or fixed-parameter tractability when \(H\) is treated as a variable input. It asks for ordinary polynomial bit complexity for each fixed class.

There is no bound on the maximum degree, clique size or biclique size of \(G\). No sparsity promise is imposed beyond the forbidden induced forest. Recognition of \(H\)-freeness can be done in polynomial time for fixed \(H\), but the optimization guarantee is required only on that class.

Computing the exact optimum value and outputting an optimum set are polynomial-time equivalent here by the usual self-reduction on induced subgraphs, which remain \(H\)-free. The primary source discusses the full family of forests; the symmetric long claws \(S_{t,t,t}\) are a central subfamily, not an unmentioned restriction of this formulation.
answer_criterion: Prove polynomial-time solvability for every fixed forest in the stated family, or refute this assertion for at least one fixed forest. Any complexity assumption used for a negative result must be explicit. A quasipolynomial-time algorithm, an approximation scheme or a theorem requiring bounded degree or a forbidden biclique does not meet the full target.
